name: Lyo.FileStorage
tagline: Save, stream-save, read, delete, and file metadata. Optional compression (Lyo.Compression), two-key encryption (Lyo.Encryption), duplicate hashing, access policies, audit hooks, multipart (IMultipartUploadService), and presigned/direct-upload/copy on cloud backends.
description:
Save, stream-save, read, delete, and file metadata. Optional compression ([Lyo.Compression](../../Compression/Lyo.Compression/README.md)), two-key encryption ([Lyo.Encryption](../../../Security/Encryption/Lyo.Encryption/README.md)), duplicate hashing, access policies, audit hooks, multipart uploads (via [IMultipartUploadService](Multipart/IMultipartUploadService.cs)), and presigned/direct-upload/copy on cloud-capable backends.

Catalog listing is `IFileMetadataStore`. Bytes go through `IFileStorageService`. Backends that can list keys expose `IFileStoragePhysical.Physical` (`IFileSystem`). `FileStorageReconcile` joins them on file id with flags `Store` / `Physical` / `Both`.

`IFileStorageTags` adds manual tags and stamps automatic `file-type` and `imported` tags. `ListTagGroupAsync` builds a virtual folder from an ordered list of tag types (including import year, month, and day) without moving object keys. `GET capabilities` includes those tag types.

With GenerateDocumentationFile set in Directory.Build.props, IntelliSense shows the same summaries as this README for documented members.

Named stores are recorded with `AddFileStorageFactory`. Inject the scoped `IFileStorageFactory` and call `Get(name)`. Disk is built in. S3, Azure Blob, FTP, and SFTP add their own builder methods. `FileStorage:Stores` binds `Provider`, plus optional `EncryptionServiceKey` and `CompressionServiceKey`. Omitted encryption passes null. Omitted compression uses the unkeyed `ICompressionService`.

sections.title: CancellationToken vs cloud signing
sections.text: ct honours cooperative cancellation during most async I/O. Presigned URL generation, some AWS signing, and synchronous SDK paths may still finish after cancellation is requested. See GetPreSignedReadUrlAsync and related remarks on IFileStorageService.

sections.title: IFileStorageService
items: **Writes.** SaveFileAsync, SaveFromStreamAsync

**Reads.** GetFileAsync, GetFileStreamAsync, GetContentIntegrityAsync (plaintext hash, algorithm, and size; no wrapped key material). Compressed payloads are decompressed via ICompressionService.Resolver using stored CompressionAlgorithm metadata. Optional per-call compressionAlgorithmOverride or FileStorageServiceBaseOptions.DecompressionAlgorithmOverride. Bounded by MaxDecompressedFileSize through MaxBytesWriteStream. OpenPlainByteRangeAsync reads one inclusive slice when SupportsPlainByteRange is true (local disk, S3, Azure Blob). FTP and SFTP leave the flag false. A plain object is sliced at the plaintext offset. An encrypted, uncompressed object is decrypted from the AEAD chunk that holds that offset, not from ciphertext byte 0. Compressed objects throw. The slice is not hash-verified.

**Zip archive.** IFileStorageArchiveService.CreateArchiveAsync spools files through Lyo.IO.Temp, zips on disk (nested ZipPath, caller fileName), and returns a stream that deletes the temp session on dispose. Caps: FileStorageArchiveOptions.MaxFileCount / MaxTotalUncompressedBytes. DI: AddFileStorageArchiveServiceFromConfiguration + AddFileStorageArchiveServiceKeyed.

**Metadata / delete.** GetMetadataAsync, DeleteFileAsync(Guid, FileDeletionMode, CancellationToken). Deletes the backing object then, depending on FileDeletionMode, either tombstones metadata (RemoveObjectAndTombstoneMetadata, default) or purges it via IFileMetadataStore.PurgeMetadataAsync (RemoveObjectAndPurgeMetadata). Operator/governance flows only. Never accept this mode from end-user input.
**Temporary links.** GetPreSignedReadUrlAsync (with optional PreSignedReadUrlOptions overrides). Both overloads accept CancellationToken, defaulting to default.
**Direct single PUT.** BeginDirectUploadAsync, CompleteDirectUploadAsync. S3/Blob fill RequiredPutHeaders for SSE + signed Content-Type parity.
**Copy.** CopyFileAsync (new file id)
**Move / rename.** MoveFileAsync (same file id, relocate by PathPrefix). RenameFileAsync changes metadata OriginalFileName only.
**Key ops.** MigrateDeksAsync, RotateDeksAsync. Results split Skipped vs Failed. Missing blobs and short encryption headers fail fast.
**Events.** FileSaved, FileRetrieved, FileDeleted, FileMoved, FileRenamed, FileMetadataRetrieved, FileAuditOccurred. Payloads carry a redacted FileStoreSnapshot (wrapped DEK and KEK salt omitted).
**Health.** CheckHealthAsync via IHealth. Depth follows HealthCheckMode.

**Capabilities.** GetCapabilities reports presigned read, direct upload, copy, move, and physical listing for this backend. Local presign follows AllowFileUriPresignedUrls. Local direct upload follows DirectUploadReceiveBaseUri. HTTP hosts add multipart, encryption, archive, and access-link flags on GET capabilities.

sections.title: IFileStorageDiagnosticsService
sections.text: Optional ListStorageKeysAsync is implemented by backends that can enumerate object/path keys (Local, S3, Blob). All implementations normalize the caller-supplied prefix through Lyo.Exceptions.FileHelpers.NormalizeAndValidatePathPrefix, the same helper that backs FileStorageServiceBase.ValidatePathPrefix. It strips wrapping slashes and rejects `..` segments, doubled separators, and embedded `\0` with ArgumentException (HTTP 400 in ASP.NET).

sections.title: Remote protocol backends (`Remote/`)
sections.body:
FTP and SFTP storage differ only in the protocol client they drive, so the storage logic lives here once and each protocol package ships a thin adapter:

- **`IRemoteFileTransport`.** The POSIX-path file operations a remote backend needs: `HealthPingAsync`, `FileExistsAsync`, `CreateDirectoryAsync`, `DeleteFileAsync`, `GetLengthAsync`, `OpenReadAsync`, `OpenCreateAsync`, `DownloadBytesAsync`, `UploadAsync`, `RenameAsync`, and `CopyFileAsync`, plus `ProtocolName` and `RootRemoteDirectory` for logs and path building. Implementations adapt a protocol library without `Lyo.FileStorage` depending on it.
- **`RemoteFileStorageServiceBase`.** A `FileStorageServiceBase` that implements every storage override (output streams, reads, deletes, size, encryption-header extraction and rewrite, partial-file cleanup, copy, move, health) against an `IRemoteFileTransport`.

Paths handed to the transport are already absolute and jailed under `RootRemoteDirectory`, so adapters do not repeat that check. Adding a protocol means implementing the transport interface and a DI extension — not another copy of the storage service.

sections.title: Multipart, direct upload, DEK operations
items: FileStorageDekOperations. Implements MigrateDeksAsync and RotateDeksAsync the same way across backends, including short-encryption-header detection and per-file failure isolation.
FileStorageStreamingPipelines. Composes compression / encryption / hash / max-size guards over streamed save and read paths.

PlainDirectUploadCoordinator. Finalizes plaintext direct-upload PUTs into a normal SaveFileAsync outcome (policy, availability) and runs only when the caller used BeginDirectUploadAsync without compression/encryption hints.
FileStorageTransfer. Copies or moves files onto another backend. MigrateDeksAsync is unchanged: it rewraps data-encryption keys inside one backend and does not move blobs or copy a key store.

sections.title: Copying or moving files (`FileStorageTransfer`)
sections.body:
`FileStorageTransfer.TransferAsync` takes a source endpoint, a destination endpoint, and a request. Each endpoint is the storage service, the metadata catalog it was constructed with, and its `IKeyStore`. `Copy` leaves the source in place. `Move` tombstones a source file only after the destination hashes match, and it never deletes source keys. Move requires a separate catalog. A shared catalog can still be copied.

`KeysOnly` copies the key versions referenced by the selected rows and does not read or write blobs. `Everything` also copies those objects. Pass `FileIds` to transfer that set. Null selects the catalog. An empty set, a missing id, a tombstone, or a pending direct upload throws before any write. `Move` with `KeysOnly` throws before any write.

`PreserveKeys` copies raw objects and the same key-encryption keys. Object keys come from `CloudObjectKeyBuilder.FromMetadata` with no storage prefix, because `IFileStoragePhysical.Physical` is already jailed to the disk root or bucket prefix. A shared catalog is left unchanged; a separate catalog receives the same `FileStoreResult`. `NewKey` mints a 32-byte key and re-saves every file with the source compression and encryption flags. `ExistingKey` re-saves under a key the destination already has and does not write key material. `KeysOnly` with either re-encrypt mode throws before any write. Re-encrypt also throws when both endpoints share one metadata instance.

A list that comes back full (`Count == ListCap`) throws before any write. `ListCap` applies only to the catalog list. Tombstones and pending direct uploads are not copied from a catalog list. A file is skipped only when the recomputed destination hashes match. A different stored `OriginalFileHash` fails that file and does not overwrite it. A missing or different stored object with the same metadata hash is rewritten, then checked again. `PreserveKeys` checks the plaintext hash and `SourceFileHash` (the bytes on disk). `NewKey` and `ExistingKey` check the plaintext hash, and the destination compression and encryption flags must match the source. A file the service will not read, such as `PendingScan`, still copies under `PreserveKeys` when the stored-object hash matches. `FilesFailed > 0` means the run did not fully succeed. Earlier destination files stay. A failed file stays on the source. Cancellation throws `OperationCanceledException`. Pass `IProgress<FileStorageTransferProgress>` to hear listing, key, file, and throttled byte progress. Null progress reports nothing. Raw copy progress uses the stored size. Re-save progress uses the plaintext size.

`GetContentIntegrityAsync` returns the plaintext hash, algorithm, and size without wrapped key material. That is the hash of a full download body.

FTP and SFTP do not implement `IFileStoragePhysical`, so `PreserveKeys` throws for them. They can still use `NewKey` or `ExistingKey`.

MaxUploadSizeBytes, MaxDecompressedFileSize, Allowed/Denied content types, file-name patterns, and sniffed types, VerifyFileSignature

Safety / validation. MaxUploadSizeBytes is enforced on direct-upload PUT bodies as well as streamed saves. For content type, file name, and sniffed type, set Allowed* (whitelist) or Denied* (blacklist), not both — ValidateUploadFilters throws ArgumentException when both sides of one pair are non-null. Null omits that side. An empty whitelist rejects everything on that dimension; an empty blacklist rejects nothing. VerifyFileSignature starts false; when true, the header must agree with the claimed type. Sniffed names are FileTypeInfo names. JAR, DOCX, and XLSX share the ZIP signature, so denying JAR denies every PK header.
DefaultAvailability is written on save when the caller does not pass an override. AllowReadQuarantinedForAdmin lets Get and presigned read open Quarantined files (admin tooling).
When set, every read decompresses with this codec instead of per-file metadata (migration/recovery).

sections.title: Upload filters
sections.body:
Each filter is a whitelist (`Allowed*`) or a blacklist (`Denied*`). Leave a property unset to skip that side. Setting both sides of one filter throws at startup.

```json
"DiskFileStorage": {
  "RootDirectoryPath": "/data/files",
  "AllowedContentTypes": [ "application/pdf", "image/png", "image/jpeg" ],
  "DeniedFileNamePatterns": [ "\\.(exe|dll|jar|bat|cmd|ps1|scr)$" ],
  "DeniedSniffedFileTypes": [ "ZIP", "RAR", "7Z" ],
  "VerifyFileSignature": true
}
```

File-name patterns match the full name and are not auto-anchored, so `\.pdf$` allows `report.pdf` and rejects `report.pdf.jar`. An unrecognized header fails a sniffed whitelist and passes a sniffed blacklist. `VerifyFileSignature` rejects `report.pdf` whose bytes start with `PK`.

sections.title: Compression resolver
rows: When compress: true, ICompressionService.ResolveForCompress picks the codec (delegates to ICompressionAlgorithmSelector when registered in compression DI). ICompressionService.Resolver performs the compress. FileStoreResult.CompressionAlgorithm records the codec.

metadata.CompressionAlgorithm → ICompressionService.Resolver.DecompressAsync. Override order: per-call compressionAlgorithmOverride → DecompressionAlgorithmOverride → metadata → ICompressionService.Algorithm (legacy rows with IsCompressed but null algorithm).

File storage depends on ICompressionService only. Register AddCompressionService + AddCompressionPolicySelector in the host. Register addon factories (LZ4, Zstd, …) for every algorithm you may read. See [Lyo.Compression](../../Compression/Lyo.Compression/README.md).

sections.title: Duplicate detection
rows: If an active row exists for the hash and the requested storage profile matches the stored row (IsCompressed, IsEncrypted, CompressionAlgorithm when compressed, DataEncryptionKeyId when encrypted, compared after write-time compression policy resolution), return that row's metadata and skip writing. If the hash matches but the profile differs, throw ConflictException (HTTP 409). Soft-deleted rows are excluded from hash lookup.

Delete the prior blob, reuse the existing file id, and save again using the new request's compress/encrypt options (profile may change: plain ↔ compressed, unencrypted ↔ encrypted, different keyId, etc.).
Always allocate a new file id even when the hash matches. Profiles may still differ.
sections.lead: When EnableDuplicateDetection is true, saves hash plaintext and call IFileMetadataStore.FindByHashAsync before persisting transformed bytes.
sections.trail:
Reads stay the same: GetFileAsync / GetFileStreamAsync decode according to stored metadata, not per-request compress/encrypt flags.

Disk options bind from the preferred section, then DiskFileStorage.

sections.title: Features
items: **Multiple storage backends.** Local disk lives in this package. Cloud lives in Lyo.FileStorage.S3 and Lyo.FileStorage.AzureBlob.
**Compression and encryption.** Optional ICompressionService (exposes Resolver and ResolveForCompress; policy via AddCompressionPolicySelector) and ITwoKeyEncryptionService.
**Metadata.** IFileMetadataStore (FileStoreResult).
**Duplicate detection.** Configurable hashing strategies via DuplicateHandlingStrategy.
**Streaming.** SaveFromStreamAsync, pipeline reads via GetFileStreamAsync.
**Lifetimes.** Honour lifetimes on IFileMetadataStore and keystores. Overlapping async calls on one service instance are supported.
**Cleanup.** Partial file cleanup helpers on FileStorageServiceBase.
**Metrics and logging.** Hooks into IMetrics / ILoggerFactory.

sections.title: Error handling
sections.text: Errors cover missing optional services, invalid prefixes, traversal attempts (diagnostics/listing paths), FileNotAvailableException for availability-aware reads, FilePolicyRejectedException for content-policy rejections, and FileNotFoundException when configured to throw.

sections.title: Security
sections.text: Path prefixes are normalised on cloud/local paths via shared helpers: Lyo.Exceptions.FileHelpers.NormalizeAndValidatePathPrefix for both listing prefixes and save/direct-upload entry points, and CloudObjectKeyBuilder for object/blob key shape (Build, FromMetadata from SourceFileName + path prefix, InferTrailingSuffixAfterFileId). Save paths also apply EnsureUnderRoot before writing to disk. HashVerifyingReadStream uses a fixed-time compare and only verifies on EOF. Pre-signed reads fall back to the metadata-recorded PathPrefix so SAS/GET URLs work even when the caller cannot supply the original prefix. DirectUploadReceiveBaseUri trusts the named host. Use only inside controlled Test API topologies.

sections.title: Concurrency
sections.text: LocalFileStorageService and FileStorageServiceBase accept overlapping async calls. Honour the lifetimes of IFileMetadataStore and keystores.

sections.title: Health checks
sections.text: Call await fileStorage.CheckHealthAsync(ct). Backends pick lightweight vs deeper modes via HealthCheckMode.

sections.title: Tests
rows: Local backend end-to-end (streaming, hashing, multipart, direct upload, audit, availability policy, duplicate strategies, cancellation, deletion modes), FileHelpers path-prefix coverage, CloudObjectKeyBuilder.FromMetadata, and zip archive (flat/nested paths, names, limits, missing id, temp-session dispose)
Isolated coverage for S3UploadServerSideEncryption, S3UploadStream, S3GetObjectResponseStream, CloudObjectKeyBuilder, options invariants
sections.trail: Cloud backends use a `DispatchProxy`-based lightweight stub for `IAmazonS3`. Deeper end-to-end coverage would need LocalStack/Azurite.
